root_cause.text: The commit that added memory clock auto-gating support introduced code in `dw_mci_rockchip_init` that unconditionally accesses the private data structure (`host->priv`) without a NULL check, while older SoCs (rk2928, rk3066, rk3188) lacked a `parse_dt` callback to allocate that private data, causing a NULL-pointer dereference.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit description state: "Commit ff6f0286c896 ... makes the private data sort of mandatory, because the init function checks whether phases are configured internally or through the clock controller. This results in the old SoCs then experiencing NULL-pointer dereferences when they try to access that private-data struct." The patch adds `dw_mci_rk2928_parse_dt` to provide the missing private data for these old controllers.

Closing brace of the init function (or a related function). Represents the end of the vulnerable code block where no NULL check was performed.

Declaration of parse_dt for rk3288. Highlights that only rk3288 and later SoCs have a parse_dt callback to allocate private data, while older SoCs (rk2928, rk3066, rk3188) lack it, leading to a NULL host->priv.
Opening brace of dw_mci_rk3288_parse_dt. This function allocates priv, but older SoCs do not have a similar parse_dt, so host->priv remains NULL.
Local variable declaration in parse_dt. Shows that rk3288 allocates priv, but without a parse_dt for older SoCs, the dereference in dw_mci_rockchip_init will access NULL.
Declaration of driver data for rk2928 without a parse_dt callback. This means host->priv is never allocated, causing a NULL-pointer dereference in dw_mci_rockchip_init.
Assignment of the common init function to rk2928. This init function unconditionally accesses host->priv without a NULL check, exploiting the missing parse_dt.
Closing of rk2928_drv_data. Confirms that no parse_dt is provided for rk2928, directly contributing to the vulnerability.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is part of the dw_mci_rockchip_init function, which unconditionally accesses host->priv earlier without a NULL check. By returning successfully after the vulnerable dereference, the function fails to bail out if priv is NULL, allowing the NULL-pointer dereference to occur earlier in the function and propagate as a crash.

Closing brace of the dw_mci_rockchip_init function (or a related function). It marks the end of the vulnerable code where no NULL check on host->priv was performed, and the function executes to completion regardless of whether priv was allocated.

Declaration of the parse_dt callback for rk3288, which allocates host->priv. Its presence highlights that only rk3288 and later SoCs have a parse_dt to allocate the private data, while older SoCs (rk2928, rk3066, rk3188) lack this callback, leaving host->priv NULL and leading to a NULL-pointer dereference in dw_mci_rockchip_init.

Opening brace of dw_mci_rk3288_parse_dt. This function is the only parse_dt implementation among Rockchip SoC variants, meaning older SoCs have no parse_dt to allocate priv, directly contributing to the NULL-pointer dereference in the common init function.

Local variable declaration inside dw_mci_rk3288_parse_dt. It shows that only this parse_dt allocates priv; older SoCs without parse_dt never allocate priv, so host->priv remains NULL when dw_mci_rockchip_init runs on those SoCs, triggering the vulnerability.

Declaration of the driver data for rk2928 without a parse_dt callback. This means the private data for this SoC is never allocated, causing host->priv to be NULL. When dw_mci_rockchip_init executes (assigned via .init), it unconditionally dereferences host->priv, leading to a NULL-pointer dereference.

Assignment of the common init function (dw_mci_rockchip_init) to the rk2928 driver data. This init function unconditionally accesses host->priv without a NULL check, exploiting the fact that no parse_dt is provided for rk2928 to allocate priv. Thus, a NULL-pointer dereference occurs.

Closing brace of the rk2928_drv_data structure. It confirms that no parse_dt callback is assigned to rk2928, directly leading to the missing allocation of host->priv and the subsequent NULL-pointer dereference in dw_mci_rockchip_init.
